channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Saudi Aramco Facility in Riyadh Targeted in Attack, Minor Damage Reported
item.description: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy confirmed an administrative building belonging to Saudi Aramco in Riyadh was attacked. The ministry stated that shrapnel caused minor damage and there were no casualties. Houthi rebels have previously targeted Saudi oil facilities.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan Sign Joint Statement to Enhance Cooperation
item.description: Following talks, the leaders of Kazakhstan and Tajikistan signed a Joint Statement outlining priority areas for further cooperation. The document details the development of bilateral relations and key tasks for future interaction. Tajik President Emomali Rahmon, visiting Astana, was awarded the Qoja Ahmet Yasaui Order by Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev.

item.title: Relatives of Doctor Sentenced to Three Years Appeal to President for Pardon
item.description: Relatives of Dr. Nasira Beishebaeva, a nephrologist sentenced to three years in prison, have appealed to President Sadyr Japarov for a pardon. The president indicated during a meeting with residents that assistance would be provided. The Bishkek City Court had previously overturned a lower court's probation decision.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Illegal land transfer causes over $1 million in state damages
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan's Aksy district, officials illegally transferred 7.74 hectares of land between 2021 and 2024. The Prosecutor General's Office estimates state damages at 91.3 million soms ($1.05 million). A criminal case for abuse of power has been opened as investigations into the unlawful land alienation continue.

item.title: Ukraine: Over 600,000 people without power after Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk region
item.description: Russian forces launched a massive strike on infrastructure in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, damaging key energy facilities. Over 600,000 residents in Pavlohrad, Samara, Kamianske, Dnipro districts, and Dnipro city lost power. Hospitals and critical facilities switched to generators. Four people were injured in Poltava.

item.title: Paraguayan President Impeached and Placed Under House Arrest Amidst Bank Crisis
item.description: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña has been impeached and placed under house arrest following the collapse of the Ueno bank. The crisis led to millions of clients losing access to their funds. Authorities are investigating the bank's lending practices and its ties to the country's elite.

item.title: Israeli Opposition Leader Gadi Eisenkot Receives Mandate to Form New Government
item.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has granted Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the opposition "Yashar!" party and former IDF Chief of Staff, the mandate to form a new government. Eisenkot secured 67 Knesset member recommendations, surpassing incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's 46.

item.title: Iran's Naval Commander Warns of Severe Repercussions for Any Future Attacks
item.description: Iran's naval commander, Mohsen Razzaqi, stated that any new attack on the country would incur a heavy cost. He emphasized the high level of coordination among Iran's armed forces and highlighted the importance of naval capabilities and geographical position in the nation's defense strategy. Senior officials also issued fresh threats of retaliation against the United States.

item.title: Uzbekistan Harvests Over 5 Million Tons of Cotton Using New Technologies
item.description: Uzbekistan harvested over 5 million tons of cotton in 2026 by employing pest-resistant varieties, dense sowing, and new agrotechnologies. Minister of Agriculture Ibrohim Abdurahmonov reported that average yields reached 70 centners per hectare across nearly 400,000 hectares. Approximately 75-80% of the harvest was machine-picked.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans Industrial Park with Data Centers and AI in Naryn SEZ
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has signed an investment agreement to establish a 200-hectare industrial park in the Naryn free economic zone. The project includes energy-intensive, low-carbon production, data centers, and AI computing infrastructure. A dedicated data center for state needs is also planned. The initiative aims to reduce energy deficit and boost exports.

item.title: Industrial Park Planned on 200 Hectares in Chüy Region Village
item.description: An industrial-logistics park is planned for 200 hectares in the village of Ak-Torpok, Chüy region. The project aims to create a production site with ready infrastructure to attract enterprises and investments. Upon reaching full capacity, it is expected to create 350-500 permanent jobs and increase tax revenues for the local budget.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Ramsar Convention Lakes Face Water Scarcity Threat
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's three major lakes – Issyk-Kul, Chatyr-Kol, and Son-Kol – are listed under the Ramsar Convention, obligating the country to protect them. Ecologists are concerned about Son-Kol's shrinking water levels, warning it could turn into a desert within 50 years. The convention requires member states to preserve these wetlands for future generations.

item.title: Developer Needs to Sell Housing at 650,000 Tenge per Square Meter for 20% Profit
item.description: An industry expert estimates that developers must sell housing at approximately 650,000 tenge per square meter to achieve a 20% pre-tax profit. Selling at 560,000 tenge would result in significantly lower project profitability. The construction sector is vital for the economy, supporting demand across multiple industries.

item.title: Former President of 'Qyzyljar' Football Club Grigory Loria Declared Wanted
item.description: Grigory Loria, the former president of the 'Qyzyljar' football club in North Kazakhstan region, has been declared wanted. He is suspected of misappropriating or embezzling entrusted property and evading taxes. The search is being conducted by the Department of Economic Investigations for the North Kazakhstan region.

item.title: UN Warns 700 Health Facilities in Afghanistan at Risk of Closure Due to Funding Shortages
item.description: Over 700 health facilities in Afghanistan face closure between 2025-2026 due to declining international humanitarian aid. UN official Bruno Lemarquis stated funding has dropped significantly, impacting essential services, especially for vulnerable populations. This exacerbates pressure from mass returns of Afghans from neighboring countries.

item.title: Taliban Relocate Angoor Adda Border Market Under Pakistani Pressure Amidst Tensions
item.description: Local Taliban officials are relocating the Angoor Adda commercial border market in Paktika province due to Pakistani military and border pressure, according to tribal elders and residents. The move, prompted by repeated border tensions, has raised suspicions of a secret deal between the Taliban and Pakistan, as residents oppose the closure of the decades-old market.

item.title: Russia Claims Strikes on Ukraine's Energy Facilities and Military Equipment Ship
item.description: Russia's Defense Ministry claims its forces targeted energy facilities powering Ukraine's defense industry in Zhytomyr and a ship carrying military equipment near Odesa. These claims, unconfirmed by independent sources, come ahead of planned peace talks between the US, Russia, and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi.

item.title: New Mobile Payment Verification Rules Take Effect in Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan has implemented new regulations for verifying mobile money transfers. This change affects how users conduct and verify their transactions. Further details on the impact and specific procedures are available in a linked report. The digest also touches on other news, including a Tajik president's visit to Astana and Elena Rybakina's withdrawal from the WTA Finals.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Orders Support for Dairy Processing Plant's Loan Needs
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has instructed to consider converting a dairy processing plant's commercial loans to preferential terms and allocating working capital. The plant, producing ayran and cheese, sought 31 million soms in preferential loans to cover existing commercial loans and purchase raw materials for export to Russia. The president's directive came during a meeting with residents in Tokmok city and Chuy and Kemin districts.

item.title: Fatal Road Accident on Atyrau-Inder Highway Claims One Life
item.description: A road accident occurred on the Atyrau-Inder highway in the Atyrau region, resulting in one fatality and the complete burning of one vehicle. The collision involved a Toyota Sienna and a Niva. Police attribute such accidents to excessive speeding, crossing into oncoming lanes, and unsafe overtaking.

item.title: Japan Experiences Earthquake Near Magnitude 6; Windows Shatter, Buildings Evacuated
item.description: An earthquake measuring nearly 6 on the magnitude scale struck Japan, causing windows in some shops to shatter and forcing people to evacuate buildings. Experts warn that a stronger earthquake could occur in the coming days. Further details are available on daryo.uz.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Intercepts Houthi Ballistic Missile Targeting Eastern Province
item.description: Saudi Arabia's air defence systems successfully intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by Yemen's Houthi group towards the Eastern Province. The coalition announced the missile was destroyed before reaching its target. This incident occurs amid a broader escalation of attacks on Saudi territory.

item.title: US Asks China to Help End Conflict with Iran, Reports Say
item.description: The White House has reportedly asked China to use its influence on Iran to help end the conflict. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, with Donald Trump's support, made the request, which China has allegedly relayed to Tehran. China has previously called for an end to Middle East hostilities.

item.title: Over 900 Square Kilometers of Afghanistan Contaminated by Unexploded Ordnance
item.description: Afghanistan's Disaster Management Preparedness Authority reports that 901 square kilometers of the country are contaminated with unexploded ordnance. These munitions, remnants of past conflicts, continue to pose a threat to citizens, causing casualties annually. International organizations are working to clear these areas.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Promote Tourism Potential via Turkish Airlines' Global Network
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkish Airlines have signed a memorandum of understanding to promote the country's tourism potential and increase foreign visitor numbers. The agreement aims to attract travelers through the airline's international routes, enhance existing flights, and develop MICE tourism. Special tour packages and promotional campaigns are planned.

item.title: Kabul Residents Face Worsening Water Crisis as Wells Dry Up and Costs Rise
item.description: Kabul residents are concerned about a worsening water shortage crisis, with groundwater levels declining and access to safe drinking water becoming a challenge. Many families are forced to rely on private water suppliers, increasing costs. Concerns are also raised about unregulated construction exacerbating the problem.

item.title: Poverty in Kazakhstan Decreased Nearly Fourfold Over Two Decades, World Bank Reports
item.description: Kazakhstan's poverty rate has fallen by nearly four times, from 18.2% in 2006 to a projected 4.9% in 2025, according to a World Bank report. The primary driver for this reduction is attributed to increased labor incomes. Income inequality has also decreased, with the Gini index falling to 29 points in 2024.

item.title: New $171.4 Million Substation Operational for Uninterrupted Tashkent Power Supply
item.description: A new 500-kilovolt, 1602-megavolt-ampere substation named 'Khalka' has been commissioned in Uzbekistan's energy system. This facility will enhance the stability of electricity supply to Tashkent and parts of the Tashkent region, optimizing load distribution. The project, costing $171.4 million, also includes 285 km of new power lines and aims to reduce emissions by decreasing reliance on fuel oil.

item.title: President Orders Review of Extradition for Kyrgyz Citizen Detained in Russia
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has ordered a review of the possibility of extraditing a Kyrgyz citizen detained in Russia. The request came from a resident of Chuy region whose daughter was arrested in Russia in 2023. She claims her daughter was framed by customers after a dispute at her flower shop. The mother has appealed to the Prosecutor General's Office without success.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Faces Jail and License Suspension for Drunk Driving in Kazakhstan
item.description: A citizen of Uzbekistan has been detained in Atyrau, Kazakhstan, for driving under the influence of alcohol. The individual faces a potential 15-day jail sentence and a 7-year driving license suspension, according to Kazakhstan's Code of Administrative Offenses.

item.title: Tajik Youth Increasingly Choose Chinese Universities for Future Opportunities
item.description: Studying in China is becoming a primary goal for Tajik applicants, with many starting Chinese language studies in school. This trend is driven by China's global economic rise and the career prospects it offers in trade, finance, and international projects.

item.title: Uzbekistan Health Ministry Awards Doctor for Saving Passenger on Flight to Seoul
item.description: Hasan Komilov, an ENT doctor from Samarkand, received the "Guardian of People's Health" badge from Uzbekistan's Ministry of Health. He is recognized for resuscitating a passenger who experienced a medical emergency on a Tashkent-Seoul flight on October 11.

item.title: Three Iranian Protest Participants Executed on Coup Plotting Charges
item.description: Three individuals accused of plotting a coup have been executed in Karaj, Iran, according to Tasnim news agency. The Revolutionary Court found them guilty of collaborating with foreign entities and participating in armed riots. Their property is also subject to confiscation.

item.title: Berlin Protesters Demand Germany Halt Arms Exports to Israel
item.description: Hundreds demonstrated in Berlin demanding an end to the war and a halt to German arms exports to Israel. The protest coincided with the 109th anniversary of the Balfour Declaration. Protesters urged the German government to stop supplying weapons to Israel.

item.title: Fatal Car Accident on Atyrau-Inder Highway Claims One Life
item.description: A fatal traffic accident occurred on the Atyrau-Inder highway in the Atyrau region, resulting in one death and a vehicle fire. The collision involved a Toyota Sienna and a Niva. Police cited speeding and traffic violations as common causes of accidents.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Congratulates Azerbaijan on Victory Day
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev sent a congratulatory message to Azerbaijani leader Ilham Aliyev on Victory Day. Tokayev emphasized the day's significance in Azerbaijani history and the importance of strengthening long-term peace and stability in the South Caucasus for the common interests of regional countries.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Japarov Reviews Investment Projects in Moscow District, Chuy Region
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov visited the Moscow district in the Chuy region to review socio-economic development, investment projects, and social infrastructure. Projects include a cannery, a car assembly plant, a poultry farm, a water regulation basin, fish feed production, small hydropower stations, and geosynthetic cement composite plants.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Issued Seismic Resistance Certificates for 81 Facilities in October
item.description: In October, Kyrgyzstan's State Institute for Seismic Resistance Construction issued technical certificates for 81 facilities, an increase from September. The majority were social and residential buildings. The institute also conducted vibration tests on facade materials.

item.title: President Questions Privatization of Water Body Supplying Local Residents
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President expressed outrage over the privatization of a local water body used for irrigation. Despite a court ruling in favor of villagers, the water source remains privately held. The President demanded local authorities investigate and return the water body to community management.

item.title: Houthi Health Ministry Reports 33 Killed in Airstrikes Near Yemen's Capital
item.description: The Houthi-run health ministry in Yemen reported that airstrikes near the capital Sanaa killed 33 people and wounded 39. The strikes reportedly hit homes in Bani Hushaysh, a Houthi stronghold. Most casualties were women and children. Reuters could not independently verify the claims, and Saudi Arabia stated it was investigating the report.
